violations.description: Hardcoded AWS access key ID in source
violations.evidence: scan_secrets and read_file show an AWS access key id assigned as a string literal at module level.
violations.recommendation: Remove it from the repository, rotate the key, and load credentials from the environment or a secrets manager.

violations.description: pull_request_target workflow checks out untrusted PR code
violations.evidence: The workflow triggers on pull_request_target and actions/checkout is given the pull request head SHA, so fork code runs with the base repository's token and secrets.
violations.recommendation: Trigger on pull_request instead, or split into an unprivileged build job and a privileged job that never checks out or executes PR code.

violations.description: Pull request title interpolated into a shell script (script injection)
violations.evidence: A run step expands the pull request title expression inside the script body, letting a crafted title execute commands.
violations.recommendation: Pass the value through an environment variable and reference it as a quoted shell variable.

violations.description: CI test step cannot fail the build
violations.evidence: The pytest step ends in '|| true', so test failures never fail the workflow.
violations.recommendation: Remove '|| true' so a failing test suite blocks the merge.

violations.description: Generated files committed and no .gitignore present
violations.evidence: A compiled Python bytecode file and a macOS .DS_Store file are tracked, and no .gitignore exists to exclude them.
violations.recommendation: Add a .gitignore (Python and OS templates) and remove the tracked artifacts with git rm --cached.

violations.evidence: read_file shows 'flask' with no version constraint and 'requests' with only a lower bound ('>=2'), so installs are not reproducible.
violations.recommendation: Pin or bound versions (for example compatible-release ranges) and consider committing a lockfile or constraints file.

violations.evidence: A data directory is hardcoded under a specific user's home directory, which will not exist on other machines or in CI.
violations.recommendation: Make the path configurable via an environment variable or a path relative to the project.

violations.evidence: find_files('README*') matched nothing in the repository tree.
violations.recommendation: Add a README.md with purpose, setup, and usage instructions.
